question: Should ClawHub enforce a 40-character maximum for new or renamed skill display names while grandfathering unchanged legacy over-limit titles across hosted publish and GitHub-backed sync?
rationale: The linked issue asks for concise titles but does not specify the exact maximum or the permanent compatibility rule for already-published long names.

options.title: Accept 40 with repaired compatibility
options.body: Keep this PR direction, but require the GitHub exact-limit repair, focused regression coverage, and real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Choose a different title policy
options.body: Ask the contributor to adjust the shared constant, UI copy, sync behavior, and tests to the maintainer-approved maximum and legacy rules.

options.title: Defer the policy
options.body: Keep the linked issue open as the policy tracker and pause or close this PR until maintainers are ready to enforce a stored catalog display-name limit.

recommendation.title: Accept 40 with repaired compatibility
recommendation.body: Keep this PR direction, but require the GitHub exact-limit repair, focused regression coverage, and real behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen has the strongest current history across the GitHub-backed sync and publish helper surfaces where the policy would land.
